label: models/fw_valvewheel.mdl: a valve wheel, red paint worn to steel at the rim

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/snapbug.mdl, models/rip.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked D, D, C, D where the asset was C, A, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The front and back views are a round wheel about 32 across, matching the brief's words, with a rim, spokes and a hub on a stem. The outline is the same in every view: the wheel is a flat disc seen edge-on from the side and top, with no part sticking out or missing. The measured size is 31.9 across.

M2.reason: The brief asks for 32 across. The asset measures 31.9 across, within 0.2%. The brief gives no depth or height, so those are not held to it. The 9-unit depth and 34-unit height are within reason for a wheel on a stem.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, down to the small ones: the rim (a tube with a polygonal, faceted outline, visible in the front and back views), the spokes (five red bars, all reaching from the hub to the rim), the hub (a red diamond block at the centre, in every view), and the stem (the brown column under the hub, in the left, right and below views). None is missing. The brief sets no count of spokes or rim sides, so none is held to one. Red paint on the spokes and hub reads at the game's size, as the brief asks.

M4.reason: The rim is bare steel grey with the red worn off it, as the brief asks. The spokes and hub are solid red. The stem is rust brown, which fits the rusted steel of the palette. Each region reads as one material in every view, with no stray colour.

M5.reason: The wear is there: the rim is speckled bare steel where the red has worn off, the spokes have streaks, and the stem has mottled rust. The detail is at a sharpness close to Half-Life's own prop textures at this size. Nothing is smeared or noisy beyond that.

M6.reason: Capped by the line-up test, as the rubric says for this judge. In the four readings the asset sat at C, A, B and D; the judges picked D, D, C and D, so only the reading with the asset at D caught it. The asset passed for one of the game's, which is the test's result.

M7.reason: The wheel faces forward in the front view, upright, with its face to the viewer. The stem stands down from the hub, so the wheel stands on its base. The brief gives no origin, so this is judged as a valve wheel standing upright.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. The asset has 194 triangles, under the 198 bound (twice the median of 99 for Half-Life's own props of this kind and size), and under the 422 most. The views show no open or inside-out faces, and nothing floats: the rim, spokes, hub and stem all join.
